utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have already told me, the information contained in this document is not what you learnt yourself directly. You drafted this document based on the reports provided to you by the teams who were aware of some facts. In other words, this was somebody else's knowledge that you put in this report. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: This is correct. And I have to add that the paragraph A, which starts on page 1, mainly is the observations of the head of the regional centre himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be returned and can the witness be shown document P155.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Residovic, we have an hourglass that monitors the time. The examination-in-chief lasted 40 minutes. How much more time will you be needing to complete your cross-examination? Today we have a little time in front of us, but we would like to stick to a certain frame. How much more time will be needed -- will you be needing to complete your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes. That's okay. Can you, then, proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown P155, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Schellschmidt, can you please look at item 19. It says here that on the 19th of May [as interpreted] in the evening the courier of the Arab Group verbally provided the ECMM with some proposals. Is it true that from that moment on in this report you list the events that you personally witnessed or were involved with -- involved in, that is to say the events during the period from the time when you took over the duties from Mr. Dagos and continued in your role as a negotiator with the foreign citizens?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: This is correct. On the 11th of May, I was in charge already, and from that moment on the report, which was written by myself, covers the events and facts that I witnessed myself, or did myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can a correction be made on page 46, line 16. It says "19th of May." And it should be 11th of May. This is a mistake in the transcript and not in what you have told us. Will you then agree with me that the events described under 1 through 19 is not your personal knowledge, but rather the information that you received from Mr. Dagos or in some other way?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Actually, it's mainly based on the information I got from Mr. Dagos. Part of it I witnessed myself. But it's correct, mainly based on the information I got before I took over.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, up to item 19, well, these are things you can't be quite certain of. You can't be certain whether the events took place as described in this report.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, actually, even if I did not witness them myself, I'm quite sure they happened as they are described.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a fact were described in some other way in Mr. Dagos's daily report, you would then accept that the way Mr. Dagos described it on the day he compiled his report was correct. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I think I have to agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Schellschmidt, thank you for answering all the questions I put to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. I have concluded my cross-examination of this witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours. A few questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura, Mr. Schellschmidt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You mentioned in your testimony that on the 14th of April you were informed by the HVO about four HVO officers being kidnapped and the circumstances of their kidnapping in the Travnik area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Would you confirm that it was your conclusion - and this is recorded in your report - that is Prosecution Exhibit 155, which can be given to you if you need a copy - but it's in paragraph 2 of your chronology of events, that your conclusion was that the persons were kidnapped by unknown persons.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, of course the persons were unknown. But as witnesses referred to that green truck, we were quite sure that members or parts of the 7th Muslim Brigade might be involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: But it was never ever proved through your investigations that any members of the 7th Brigade were involved in this kidnapping, and hence in your report you indicate that the persons who perpetrated the act were unknown; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Mr. Schellschmidt, can you confirm that from your entire experience in the exchange process, that it was the members of the Arab Group, as you put it, and their chief negotiator that laid down the demands for the release of the foreign prisoners and negotiated through your offices, through the ECMM, for their release from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And it was the members of that group that requested meetings with the various organisations in Zenica, including the HVO, the 3rd Corps, the 7th Brigade and other organisations based in Zenica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: It's right, except that I'm not aware of any request to have a representative of 7th Brigade included into this negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So the request was to have members from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Of the 3rd Corps, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Referring to your report again that was shown to you earlier on - that's Prosecution Exhibit P155 - there was, however, and this is mentioned at paragraph 12 of your report, there was, however, a visit made by the ECMM to the 7th Brigade. And can you confirm that the 7th Brigade requested that a meeting be held on this issue with the HVO, the 3rd Corps, and various other organisations based in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, I have to state that I was not part of the group that visited the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: This visit was done to my memory by Mr. Thebault himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: So I'm not in a position to confirm any specific request from the side of the 7th Brigade in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: But if such a meeting was held by Ambassador Thebault, it would be entirely appropriate that it be put in your report, as I have mentioned, at paragraph 12 even though you might not have attended that meeting.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a group of soldiers - you weren't able to identify any insignia on the soldiers - that were outside of the Hotel Internacional at various places. You never had an opportunity to speak to those soldiers or any commander of those soldiers on the scene, did you?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: No, I did not have an opportunity to talk to any of them, but we of course realised when the whole crew left, they went towards the barracks of the headquarters of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: When they left, they left in various vehicles, did they not?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You did not follow those vehicles to where they ended up, did you?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You were shown Prosecution Exhibit 264, which you confirmed that you authored and signed. In this regard, can I confirm that the music school in Zenica was not a location that you visited personally on any occasion and you never interviewed any prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: It's correct. I never visited the prisoner in the so-called music school, but it was visited to my recollection by Mr. Thebault.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Schellschmidt. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. Does Ms. Benjamin have any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution doesn't have any re-examination at this point in time. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now consult the Judges to see whether they have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: There's only one question less for me to put to you, Witness, concerning the exchange of prisoners in Zenica between the different groups. You said in response to questions from several parties "I couldn't see any insignia on them." But then you said also, "They appeared to me to belong to the 7th army." And I would like to have an explanation of that remark. How did you arrive at that impression or conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was not referring to 7th army. If this was my words, it was a misspelling. I was referring to 7th Brigade. The conclusion was based on the fact that this vehicle, this truck-mounted four-barrelled gun, was known to us as being part of the equipment of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I wanted to refer to the 7th Brigade, of course.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm mistaken in talking about the 7th army. So that was the basis of your conclusion, you saw the weaponry and you thought this must be the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: And we saw them leaving in the direction of the barracks of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Was that close to the place or ...?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: How far was that?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Less than a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Hmm?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Less than a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay. Were there any other characteristics that would plead in favour or against assuming that this was the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Showing green flags was also a sign of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Was that a sign of people belonging to the 7th Brigade or not belonging to the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: It was specifically used by the 7th Brigade because it's the colour of the Muslim faith, of course, but it has been -- it's often shown by the brigade. And what -- I've seen it on one of the vehicles that transported the hostages from the spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You described the group of persons as soldiers. When you look at these photos that have been shown to you, you might be inclined to think that this is military dress, so to speak. Is that a correct impression from the photos?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, but at that time, Your Honour, the troops in the area were wearing different kinds of uniforms, taken from whatever stocks that were available. So everybody, you know, wearing green or camouflage uniforms and carrying a weapon we considered to be a soldier at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: What do you mean by "everybody"? That everybody belonging to the army or every person you met in a uniform or -- what is "everybody" in this respect?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: In this respect, "everybody" would be a person showing up in a group of people wearing the same type of clothing and being armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to know something about the photographs. There's the photograph of a masked soldier. Who are they? Why are they masked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will ask the registrar to provide us with the photographs again, please. Colonel, you have heard the question put to you. Could you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, please. I actually am not in a position to give the real reason why they were masked, but I assume that they did not want to be identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But which army were they part of?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: As I said earlier, we assumed that they were part of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also have a few questions for you, because there are a certain number of questions we would like to ask about the photographs. But it's not just the photographs I would like to ask you about. The Defence showed you these photographs taken from the rooftop of the Internacional Hotel. At the time of the exchange, did you think that there were people who were able to take photographs or make a report? What could you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was part of the agreement that no photographs would be taken, no press would be involved, so when I first learned about these pictures, I was quite surprised. But I cannot exclude that somebody was able - probably not from the roof but out of the window of one of the hotel rooms - to take pictures without being seen or identified. Actually, I don't know who actually took these pictures. I have some suspicions, but I cannot prove it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can see you in a photograph; you said so yourself. You can be identified. You have a walkie-talkie. Who were you in contact with? You had means of communication. Who was at the end other of the line?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: On the other end of the line was the other ops officer at that time, Mr. Remi Landry, inside the hotel building, whom I had to confirm that things were running well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the other officer was present in the building and you coordinated action with him via the walkie-talkie. So his task was to ensure that everything was running smoothly.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: On his side, yes. And the radio also was used to communicate with the British liaison officer, who was normally inside one of the armoured personnel carriers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the photographs and following the question put to you by Madam Judge, we can see that there are masked soldiers and soldiers who don't have anything on their heads -- over their heads. We can see that some have beards and we can also see that there are other soldiers without beards. Did you see any soldiers or people dressed as soldiers without beards at the site, at that place?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Not everybody being a member of the 7th Brigade was wearing a beard [Realtime transcript read in error: "badge"] Many did, but not all of them. I'm sorry, I see on the screen is translation is badge. I'm talking about a beard. Probably I misunderstood the question of the Court. Badges, I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am speaking about beards and not about badges. You are telling us that there were 7th Brigade soldiers who didn't have beards.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: As I said, not everybody being a member of the 7th Brigade was wearing a beard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite categorical when you answered questions about the lorry in which there were a number of soldiers, and we can also see a weapon which you described as an anti-aircraft weapon in a report. You said that this lorry, this truck, belonged to the 7th Brigade. What were the grounds for make such a claim? Why did you say that in your opinion there was a link to the 7th Brigade? We can't see a number plate on the truck. We have the impression that it is a civilian truck, and we have the impression that a weapon was mounted on the truck. But you are a colonel, a military specialist, so why do you claim that this truck belonged to the 7th Brigade? What are the grounds upon which you draw this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: The grounds are the fact that this vehicle has been seen on the premises of the 7th Brigade for several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Was this weapon on one of the pictures or not?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, it was on one of the pictures, on the bottom left side, but mainly covered by men standing around it on the truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as this truck is concerned - and there is in fact a flag on it - had you already seen this flag?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: For the moment, I'm not aware of that flag on that car. Perhaps I may see the picture again in order to be able to identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll show it to you. I could even put it on the ELMO -- we could even put it on the ELMO and it will be possible for everybody to see it again. It's the first truck. As you can see, there is a green flag and something is written on it. Have you already seen such a flag?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes. We -- I've seen this flag before, and although I'm not able to read Arabic, I think it was the same flag that was permanently flown by units of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have only two other questions for you, two different kinds of questions, so we can have the photograph back. The Defence presented a report from Ambassador Thebault. The Trial Chamber will decide later on whether it should be admitted or not, but you were shown this report. There are two paragraphs I would like you to comment on, since you were part of this European mission and you were in the field. In one of the paragraphs, it says that assistance, aid, was delivered to Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was either in financial, military means, or it was either in the form of weapons. The person who drafted the report said that this had a political price, and it meant that it was necessary to accept Muslim units who provided support because these countries provided funds. What is your opinion of this claim made by this ambassador, who seems to establish a link between providing weapons and funds with the presence of foreign combatants in the field? Did you discuss this matter among yourselves? And you were present, because you were there; you were in the field. What was your opinion of this, of this link established between the presence of foreign combatants and the delivery of aid?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Your Honours, this question has been discussed between us at several occasions, and I personally fully support the statement of Mr. Thebault in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: At the end of the report there are certain provisional conclusions reached by Ambassador Thebault. The following is said in these conclusions - and I would like to hear what you have to say about this because you worked with the author of this report and you certainly have an opinion - he says that "Many officers from the JNA, many former JNA officers are persuaded that the Secret Services from Serbia are involved in spreading false information." And in order to explain what the Serbian Secret Service might be engaged in, he says that it is in fact "easy to burn down unoccupied villages at night or to act like Mujahedin." That is a hypothesis that is put forward. But it seems to give one the impression that the Serbs might act by taking on the guise, in a certain sense, of Mujahedin. What is your opinion of this?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I think this assessment is correct as well, but this -- we also assessed that they did the same towards the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I reread this paragraph concerning -- if we take this together with the photographs of the exchanges, would it be possible that the Serbs had the uniforms that we can see in the middle of the town?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I cannot -- do not believe that any Serbs would be able to enter Zenica at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Would the Defence like to ask the witness any other questions, in the light of the questions put by the Judges with regard to the photographs and the various reports? Mrs. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Schellschmidt, during the exchange you didn't speak to any of the individuals wearing masks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't speak to any of the individuals who weren't masked or to any individuals who were on that truck.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: It's correct as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your claim, according to which they could have been members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, is only based on your assumptions, the assumptions you made about the truck and the direction that they followed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes. I have no other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned green flags. Would it be correct to say that at the time because of strength of religious sentiments, it was possible to see green flags in other places and on other facilities? It's not as if we could only see flags that members of the 7th Muslim Brigade used.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I said that the Hotel Internacional is at least 3 kilometres away from the headquarters of the 7th Muslim Brigade, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, earlier I estimated it to be 1 kilometre, but I'm not too sure about that. If you say it's 3, okay; it's probably 3. You know the area probably better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question, Mr. Schellschmidt: Is it true that Mujahedins and members of the BiH army, especially the 7th Muslim Brigade, were most often linked as being an item by members of the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, in a conversation with Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Dzemal Merdan, they always clearly told you that the 3rd Corps had nothing whatsoever to do or had any form of control over the Mujahedin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: That's what they told us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no other questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give the floor to Mr. Dixon, but before that, my colleague Judge has another question and then I'm going to give the floor to Ms. Residovic or Mr. Dixon, if they wish to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when I asked you why the soldiers were masked, you told me that they were masked so that they were not recognised. Why didn't they want to be recognised, since they belonged to the same brigade, the 7th Brigade? Some were not masked and the others were. Why were these others masked? Why didn't they want to be recognised?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really not in a position to answer this question. It would be just guessing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the exchange, were there any Mujahedin there on the spot?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Obviously, yes; at least, the speaker of the group which was my immediate contact was at the ground, as it is said -- demonstrated on one of the pictures. I'm not able to tell who else among the other groups was to be considered Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All but your contact. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm giving the floor to the Defence counsel for their intervention.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It won't be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Only a few questions arising from the questions that Your Honours have posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Firstly, Mr. Schellschmidt, would you agree with me that you never ever visited the 7th Brigade headquarters or its barracks?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Did you know that the headquarters and the barracks were situated at the place in Zenica called Bilmiste?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I don't recall the name, but I recall the -- the area. It was on the other bank of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: On the other side of the river.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, it would be correct, then, that you never would have had the opportunity to see this four-barrelled gun that you've mentioned at the headquarters or at the barracks of the 7th Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I didn't see it at the headquarters, because I'd never been there, but I'd seen it on the street being moved around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Is this something that you had spoken to your colleagues about, this particular gun?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes. We spoke about it, and we were quite clear in our judgement who it belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So would it be correct that you got your information from speaking to your colleagues about this equipment?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that you had seen this particular gun in one of the photographs on a vehicle, a truck, in the lower left-hand corner of the photograph; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I wonder if you could be shown, Mr. Schellschmidt, that particular photograph. The number ...

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I think it's number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's photo number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Is that the particular gun there that you say you'd spoken to your colleagues about?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, looking at the photograph very closely, that sticking out from the various soldiers sitting on the back of that truck is a single-barrel gun?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I think I can recognise at least two barrels here. It's very difficult to recognise, because as a picture --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: If you look at the photograph closely and say how many barrels you can identify, please.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Okay. There's one which always attaches the earth-moving machine which is next to it. This is definitely recognisable.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that there's only one barrel on this particular gun?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yeah. But there's another -- as you put these questions now, I'm not sure about that, because there's another vehicle just to the left which is a similar type, the same type. I'm not sure what's on that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: The vehicles to the left, would you agree they appear to be civilian vehicles of a construction nature?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, they're actually the same type and the same colour as the vehicle with the gun on the back and the soldiers on the back. No, at that time it was not possible to recognise a vehicle being military or not military because they were just taken from whatever resources which were available.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: But you would agree with me that the gun that we see in this picture is not a four-barrelled gun.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm helpfully pointed out by my legal assistant that when the photograph is zoomed in, as it is now, it might be possible to have a closer look at that second truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Mr. Schellschmidt, would you agree with me that the second truck in the bottom left-hand corner appears to be a civilian vehicle and one which does not have a flat back like the one where the soldiers are sitting on?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Obviously yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you. The photograph can be taken from the witness. There are no further questions with regard to that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to ask Mr. Registrar to give us a sub-numbering for every photo. Within that one number, can you give us a number for each of the photos, a subset of numbers, and can you please tell us for each photo what number it is so that everybody can locate every -- each particular photo in the bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe you could stick to the order that the Defence has introduced for these photos, which was very simple. For example, photo number 1 depicted two vans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe you could give us a different number for different photos. Maybe that would be the simplest way to do. Madam Usher, can you please put all the photos on the ELMO one after another, and we are going to give each of them a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may indicate that there were one or two further questions I wanted to ask, but it's certainly most --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a minute, as soon as we give each of these photos a number. This is number one, and the number one depicts two vehicles, one of them green and another one white, and there is also a white flag and a blue flag. Can we have a number for this photo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be DH183, tab 1. Sorry, I apologise: It was DH182, tab 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The second photo, please. Turn it around. In this photo, we can see a white van and there's another vehicle next to it. What number will we give to this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number is DH182, tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Number three. We can see the mediator. And the number is ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number is DH182, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next one, please. The photo was taken from above. We can see a very modern football stadium. A number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH182, tab 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number five, please. We can see a white UN vehicle, and what is the number for this photo, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH182, tab 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Photo number six, still the same vehicle with the vehicle of the United Nations and some individuals around the white vehicle. [In English] Next.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH182, tab 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the last photo, please. This photo depicts a lorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH182, tab 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had to be precise on this. Mr. Dixon, now you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And if I can confirm that the photograph that I showed the witness was indeed the photograph with tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Mr. Schellschmidt, only a few further questions, and that is: Would you agree with me that at the time the green flag or variants of the green flag were used by a number of units in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes, I have to agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You said that you assumed that the soldiers that you saw present outside the hotel were soldiers from the 7th Brigade, and you've indicated that the four-barrelled gun, for example, was one of the reasons that you used to reach that assumption. Can you confirm that after the event you never verified your assumption and were not able to confirm who the soldiers were after the event had occurred?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: No, I had no chance to verify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Schellschmidt. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now to the Prosecution. Do you have any questions arising from the Judges' questions and from the questions by the Defence? Mrs. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Colonel, in your opinion - and you have seen the pictures that were shown to you - in your opinion, when would have these -- when would have these pictures been taken? At the beginning of the exchange, during the exchange, or upon the completion of the exchange?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I assume that these pictures have been taken towards the end of the exchange, close to the moment when the hostages have been taken from the scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You indicated to us that the soldiers that you saw were from the 7th Muslim Brigade. Would you be able to give us a number as to about approximately how many soldiers were there that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your claim is not exactly what he said. He didn't say that they were. He said that they could have been. It was not really an affirmative answer, and that's why the Defence counsel would like to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This would have been my objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you rephrase your question, Mrs. Benjamin, and please be cautious.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. And sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I'll put it this way: When you got to the site of the exchange, did you see any civilian police in the area?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you see any military police in the area?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Not any recognisable military police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you see any 3rd Corps soldiers in the area?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: As there were -- as none of the persons on the scene was wearing any badges, it was impossible to establish their affiliation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But you would have seen 3rd Corps soldiers in the area before, wouldn't you have?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And at that time, would you have been able to distinguish between the 3rd Corps and soldiers of other units, including the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, normally the members of the 3rd Corps were members of the staff of the corps and most of them were known to us by face.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And at that time, you didn't see any of those in the area.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Your base, where you were based at the Internacional Hotel, could you tell us if it was close to any unit -- the base of any military unit.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Well, it was not too far from the 3rd Corps headquarters; only two or three blocks away.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And when you were standing at the point of exchange, was it possible for you to see the base of any other unit? Could you see the buildings?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: How many trucks would you have -- would you say were on the scene at the time of the exchange?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Actually, I cannot give you an exact number, but there were several trucks because the place next to the football stadium was normally used to park trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So there would have been more than the two trucks that you would have seen in the picture here today.

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: Yes. In one of the pictures you saw at least one or two trailers being parked next to the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And could you tell us in those trucks who were in the trucks?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: In the other trucks parked there, normally was nobody in the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that the two trucks that were in the picture, the only two trucks that had military persons in it?

utterances.speaker: DIETER SCHELLSCHMIDT
utterances.text: I can confirm only one truck, the one with the gun mounted in the back.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That will be all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Both Defence counsel were on their feet. If there are no other questions, Colonel, the Chamber would like to thank you for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. You have answered all the questions put to you both by the Prosecution and the Defence teams. You have also answered the questions put to you by the three Judges. We would like to thank you once again for your contribution. We would like to wish you a very safe return to your country, and we wish your retirement to be as pleasant as possible. We are going to ask Madam Usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, we have a few more minutes. We are approaching to the break. But if you have nothing to add, maybe we can adjourn earlier. What about tomorrow? What is the plan for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution has -- the witness who is currently scheduled to be available tomorrow, Hendrik Morsink, will be available tomorrow morning at 0900. Mr. President, I might also add that as we had previously indicated, the Prosecution will be making an oral application for two witnesses to be heard via videolink from Sarajevo next week, testifying the 2nd through the 4th of June. I have reason to believe that all of the translations for the medical documentation concerning those witnesses might be available. I do not have that documentation with me in the courtroom, and as of yet that documentation has not been provided to the Defence. Given time constraints, Mr. President, and particularly as it relates to the technical side, the AV Department and the Registry, the Prosecution would like to put our views with respect to the videolink motion, oral motion, if you will, before the Trial Chamber as soon as possible. Assuming that the translations are available, we could do that after a break of 15 to 20 minutes. Now, I understand, of course, my learned friends from the Defence do not have those documents yet, so they probably would not be in a position to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Alternatively, as my co-counsel points out, Mr. President, we can do that first thing in the morning, again assuming that we have those translations. I certainly don't want to lose any time. But clearly the Defence will need some time in order to respond, based on the documentation that we'll provide them. So we leave it to the Chamber whether you'd like to adjourn for the day or whether you'd like us to put our views forward with respect to the videolink motion later this evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The only question that we have with regard to the videolink conference and in the light of this Tribunal's jurisprudence, the sole question concerns the medical certificates. You said that you have these certificates but they haven't been translated. I assume that the medical certificates are in B/C/S, so it is quite possible for the Defence to familiarise themselves with these certificates, since they know the language. And the other question is that if you are in a position to provide the medical certificates in the next few minutes - perhaps you have them at hand - in such a case, the Defence might be in a position to express their position after having examined these certificates, because the Defence's position can only be based on the contents of the medical certificates. So my question is: Do you have them with you or would you have to go and fetch the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to let my co-counsel, Ms. Benjamin, address you on this point, as she'll be the one who will actually be making the oral application.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the moment there'll be two applications or an application with respect to two witnesses. With respect to witness number 1, the translation is already done and we have it in our possession. With respect to witness number 2, we have been informed a while ago that the translation has been completed. It means that we have to collect it. So I think maybe during the break we might be able to collect it and distribute it to the Defence and we might be able to do it this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would it be possible for the Defence to tell us what their position is after having examined the medical certificates? Mrs. Residovic, you're not a doctor. We aren't doctors either, but...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But it is necessary for us to see those documents, first of all. As you know, we have already had a discussion that concerned medical documents, and although we weren't doctors, we were able to assume that all the documents were rapidly received from one doctor, and this is what the Trial Chamber decided and they then took the appropriate decision. We really do need to examine the documents and, if necessary, to check what they state. After the break, we could tell the Trial Chamber whether we can tell you what our position is or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As for the other Defence team, Mr. Ibrisimovic, you're not a doctor but you are very familiar with medical documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We will be able to tell you what our position is as soon as we have examined the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The best thing to do then is to have a 15-minute break, a short break. This will give the Prosecution enough time to collect the medical certificates, provide them to the Defence, and in 15 or 20 minutes' time we will resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go into private session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're now in open session. But we don't have any documents before us -- I have the document here. I am listening to what you have to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was wondering, since this concerns his medical condition, whether we should not go back into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If you wish, we'll go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, we have one last issue to deal with, and this concerns the request made by the Defence to have the report of the -- concerning the report of the Ambassador Thebault. The Trial Chamber deliberated during the break, and we have decided to admit this document into evidence. Could the registrar give us an exhibit number, a DH number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number for the English version gets the exhibit -- the English version gets the exhibit number DH183; and the French translation gets the exhibit number DH183/F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Are there any other items on the agenda? I'll hand this document back. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing else for today, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence has no other issues to raise either?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Nothing further, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's almost time to adjourn, so we will now adjourn and I will see everyone at the hearing at 9.00, and we will render our oral decision as soon as we start the hearing tomorrow at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.47 p.m.,
